meta.description: PATH-001 (from Module 08), annotated for TIERING. Each hop records which tiering control would KILL it and the precondition that control removes. The migration's job is to make `path_open` evaluate to false for every hop, in waves, without breaking the legitimate logons in baseline.json.
meta.name: Low-priv Finance user to Domain Admin

precondition.comment: svc-mssql has an SPN and an RC4-crackable password. Out of scope for tiering per se (Module 10 hardening fixes this) — present so the path is realistic. Tiering does NOT close this hop.
Attacker now has a foothold on the Finance pilot workstation.

THE BROWNFIELD HOP. Because tallen (a Domain Admin / Tier 0) logs on INTERACTIVELY to FIN-WS01 (Tier 2), a Domain-Admin credential is sitting in LSASS on a workstation the attacker controls. secretsdump/lsass-dump yields tallen's material. CLOSE THIS by denying tallen interactive+RDP logon on the Tier 2 host (SeDenyInteractiveLogonRight / SeDenyRemoteInteractiveLogonRight) and/or putting tallen in Protected Users.

closes_when.comment: Either deny BOTH logon rights on the host, OR add tallen to Protected Users (which makes the cached credential non-harvestable). The checker treats Protected-Users membership as also closing this hop.

precondition.comment: With tallen's Domain-Admin credential the attacker DCSyncs DC01 and owns the domain. This hop is only reachable if step 3 succeeded — so killing step 3 kills the path end to end.
